moved.sentence: **Lifecycle callback implementations are natural scope group anchors.** Files that implement `UIApplicationDelegate`, `AndroidApplication`, or equivalent are the entry points of the application — they are architectural seams where scope groups plug in.

judged.note: should-anchor-groups-on-lifecycle-callbacks keeps UIApplicationDelegate/AndroidApplication implementers as natural anchors and architectural seams; the rationale keeps that they are the application's entry points.

moved.sentence: **Each OS integration point is a potential boundary.** A file that handles push notification payloads is in the notification scope group.

judged.note: should-treat-each-os-integration-point-as-distinct keeps each integration point as a potential boundary and its sub-item keeps push-notification payload handlers in the notification group.

moved.sentence: Treat each OS integration point as a distinct concern.

judged.note: should-treat-each-os-integration-point-as-distinct keeps treating each OS integration point as a distinct concern (unkeyed, now SHOULD).

moved.sentence: **Background execution code belongs in its own scope group.** Background tasks have distinct lifecycle, resource, and testing constraints.

judged.note: should-give-background-code-own-group keeps background code in its own group; the rationale keeps the distinct lifecycle, resource and testing constraints.

moved.sentence: Code that runs in background contexts should not be mixed with foreground UI code.

judged.note: should-not-mix-background-with-foreground-ui keeps the should-not at SHOULD NOT.

moved.sentence: **IPC code is infrastructure.** An app extension that communicates with its host app via shared container is infrastructure-layer code — it should be grouped with other infrastructure, not with the feature it serves.

judged.note: should-group-ipc-with-infrastructure keeps the shared-container app-extension example as infrastructure code grouped with infrastructure, not with the feature it serves.

moved.sentence: **Lifecycle callbacks that dispatch to many subsystems are composition roots.** An `AppDelegate` that calls 15 different services is a composition root, not a feature — it belongs in an `App` or `Bootstrap` scope group that wires everything together.

judged.note: should-place-composition-roots-in-bootstrap-group keeps the many-subsystem dispatcher (AppDelegate calling 15 services) as a composition root, not a feature, placed in an App or Bootstrap group.
